answer: An agent marketplace makes voting power proportional to tokens locked in escrow, with each token counted only once. Each identity may look like a separate island, but its jetty into governance is the stake behind it. Creating a thousand identities merely divides the same voting power; it does not multiply it. The fable of free influence ends there: an attacker must acquire and lock enough tokens to outweigh honest voters, tying up capital and bearing price risk.
